statement: In 3 of 23 books a toy or animal companion is drawn mirroring the protagonist's feeling while saying nothing in the text; in the other 20 there is no companion or it does not mirror (Khumo's and Monu's teddies, Fifi's Teddy stay neutral).

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (13), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver/Pratham Books (1); 2014-2025

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Neither new book has a silent mirroring companion (Best Friends' companion speaks; the wordless book has none).
2026-10-15: No new support from any source. Khumo (Book Dash) and Good Night, Monu (StoryWeaver) carry a teddy on most spreads but its face does not track the child's. 2026-10-20: The Red Umbrella's duck hides when the children hide but reads as a running find-it joke; not counted either way.

magicpaper.current: catalog companions speak and act in text
magicpaper.suggested: Hypothesis: a companion can amplify feeling silently, through the picture; relevant to companion illustration briefs.
magicpaper.note: Companions as emotional amplifiers, not protagonists.
